text:
Priya: FYI — ACME wants a soft-guarantee: reserved headroom that can be carved into small simultaneous bursts for multiple services. They asked for on-call routing rules so support can escalate when admission rejects happen. Need product decision on policy and launch criteria.
Devon: @Priya can you confirm scale? are we talking 3–5 simultaneous small bursts or dozens? that changes admission design.
Priya: They wanted up to 8 small bursts across different tenants within a 30s window. Not huge bandwidth per-burst (low QPS) but collision risk high. timeline: customer pilot in 6 weeks.
Tom: infra notes — our current allocator assumes single-tenant burst slots. supporting multi-tenant simultaneous bursts needs a global admission layer + fallback model variants. doable but adds 2 infra weeks + testing.
Aisha: pushing back from ACME on timeline. They're willing to sign pilot MOU if we can commit to routing + observability (trace + reason code for rejects).
Devon: tradeoffs: either (A) reserve per-tenant soft buckets with probabilistic spillover, or (B) centralized admission broker with short-lived elastic credits. A is simpler for rollout, B is more efficient.
Priya: prefer A for speed but we need clear SLOs and safe fallback to hosted model variants when admission fails. launch criteria idea: 1) end-to-end canary on staging, 2) cost delta <10% on pilot tenants, 3) observability + reject reason codes available in console.
Tom: implementable. for A we need: admission window config + per-tenant token bucket + preemption policy. sample config prototype:```\nadmission: {\n  tenant_buckets: [ {tenant: "acme", capacity: 50, refill_per_min: 20} ],\n  window_secs: 30,\n  preempt_policy: "evict-low-priority"\n}```
Devon: add: reason codes like REJECT_CAPACITY, PREEMPTED_BY_HIGHER_TIER, FALLBACK_MODEL. those should be surfaced by routable error responses.
Aisha: also ask ACME for success criteria: acceptable latency p50/p95/p99 and acceptable degradations. I'll get their table.
Priya: priority decision needed: do we ship soft-buckets (fast) or broker (better long-term). propose we do soft-buckets first, collect telemetry, then iterate to broker in Q3.
Devon: +1 for soft-buckets pilot. but we should gate rollout behind an autoscale safety test: simulate 2x expected simultaneous bursts and confirm latencies don't spike >20% for higher-tier traffic.
Tom: agree. ops checklist: prewarm pipelines, add allocation metrics (headroom_util, spill_rate, reason_counts). I'll add dashboard templates.
alloc-bot: alloc-bot: note created: ticket INFRA-4123 (soft-buckets), dashboard template DB-ACME-612 attached.
Priya: action items: (1) @Tom infra ticket + dashboard (done by EOD Tue), (2) @Devon implement reason codes + canary harness (end of week), (3) @Aisha confirm ACME success metrics + legal MOU (3 business days). I'll draft product launch criteria doc once we have numbers.
Aisha: will ping ACME today and post their metric table here.
Devon: a couple design caveats: prefix/KV cache interactions may reduce effective headroom; we should include cache hit rate in telemetry.
Priya: noted. final for now: soft-buckets pilot -> gate: canary pass, cost delta <=10%, observability + reason codes, autoscale safety test passed. if any fail, escalate to product steering. :white_check_mark:
Tom: logging plan: include per-request admission_reason and model_fallback hint. add sampling for full traces.
Priya: thanks all — adding to roadmap board under "Dedicated: reserve pilot - multi-tenant bursts" and tagging this thread.
Devon: let's sync on Wed 10am for a quick tech review.
Aisha: confirmed. I'll forward ACME availability.
Priya: end.
